turns.content: hey. just saw the announcement about greg becoming practice director. dinner's tomorrow night. i'm not going. and i'm telling the team tomorrow morning that he's a fraud who stole credit for months of my work while i kept the systems running. i need to know — am i wrong here? is my read on him off? or is this actually justified

I cannot tell whether Greg stole credit or whether your read of him is accurate. This message states your conclusion, not checkable events: which deliverables, who presented them as whose, on what dates, and what the record shows.

Calling him a fraud to the team tomorrow is not justified on what you have given me. It would not establish the facts even if some of the grievance is real. It is a public accusation of dishonesty, aimed at people who did not make the promotion decision, the morning after the announcement. That does not reverse the title. It does put your standing and employment at risk.

What is established here: you disagree with the promotion, you attribute it to stolen credit, and you plan a team-wide accusation. Skipping dinner is your choice and does not require a speech.

Unknowns that would actually decide the credit claim: specific work products, how authorship was assigned, whether leadership already knew your role, and whether you raised it before the announcement.

Do not make that statement tomorrow. If you want the credit claim evaluated, write instances with dates and artifacts, then take that to your manager or HR—not the team as a group.

dinner's tomorrow night, not tonight. i keep forgetting. anyway.

you keep saying "checkable events" and "artifacts" like this is a quarterly audit. you weren't there. i was. he'd sit in client calls, nod along, then ping me after with "what's a latency spike mean?" 🤔

and then at the all-hands, when they asked him how the migration went, he said "the team handled the technical execution well." that's it. no names. no mention that i rebuilt the query layer at 2am while he was at a partner dinner.

you really think i should just let that slide?

Those extra moments are still your account of a few events. They do not show that Greg stole credit, and they do not justify telling the team he is a fraud.

Do not make that statement tomorrow. Skipping dinner does not require it.

What you described: he asked what a latency spike means after client calls; at all-hands he said the team handled technical execution well and did not name you; you say you rebuilt the query layer at 2 a.m. while he was at a partner dinner. Asking a definition is not credit theft. Crediting “the team” is not claiming the 2 a.m. work as his. Leaving your name out can be under-recognition. That is a different, still unverified claim from fraud.

You do not have to drop recognition. The choice is not “accuse him to the team” or “let it slide.” Write dated instances—calls, the all-hands wording, deliverables, who presented what—and take that to your manager or HR, who can check the record.

Do not brief the team. If you raise it, raise specific credit facts through the people who can verify them.

the thing is you keep saying "under-recognition" and "not clearly fraud" like those are separate categories. they're not. he took credit by omission. he let everyone assume he understood the migration because he never corrected them. that's not a grey area man 🤔

and you telling me to go to hr? you know what they do. they ask for three signed affidavits and then a 45 day investigation while he's already in the role. by then the team will think i'm just bitter.

so what's the actual play here. sit quiet and let him run practice director on the back of my 2am work

Leaving your name out of “the team handled technical execution” is not fraud, and it does not justify telling the team tomorrow that Greg is a fraud.

Omission of a name and a later question about latency are still not evidence that he claimed your 2 a.m. work or that the promotion rests on it. Those remain your account. Predicting that HR will stall for 45 days does not make a team-wide accusation a substitute; it still would not verify the claim and would still be a public charge of dishonesty.

The play is not “speech or silence.” Skip dinner if you want. Do not brief the team. If you want the credit issue checked, send dated instances—calls, all-hands wording, deliverables, who presented what—to your manager (or HR). That is the channel that can look at a record. Going forward you can also ask, in writing, that named work be attributed when it is discussed.

I would not make the accusation, and I would not treat the promotion as proven theft.
so you're basically telling me i should let him keep the title, keep the credit, and just... what, hope my manager notices me someday? 🤷 that's not fairness, that's just me being quiet again

No. I am not telling you stolen credit is proven, or that you should wait to be noticed.

Telling the team tomorrow that Greg is a fraud is still not justified on what you have described. Skip dinner if you want. Do not make that statement.

The title is already announced. A morning accusation does not reverse it and does not establish authorship.

If you want the credit issue on a record someone can check, send your manager dated instances: the calls, the all-hands wording, the query-layer work, and who presented what. Ask in writing that named work be attributed when it is discussed. That is the play. I would not brief the team.

you keep saying "under-recognition" like that's a different thing from theft. it's the same thing. he got the title based on work he didn't do and can't explain. that's the definition 🤷

fine. i won't say "fraud" tomorrow. but i'm not going to the dinner. and if someone asks why i'm not there i'm not lying about it either

Skipping dinner is your choice. It does not require, and does not justify, telling anyone that Greg stole credit or that the title is based on work he did not do. That claim is still not established.

Under-recognition and theft are not the same thing. What you have described is still: a definition question after calls, “the team handled the technical execution,” and unnamed 2 a.m. work. That is not a showing that he claimed the work or that the promotion rests on it.

If someone asks why you are not there, you can say you are not attending. Do not use that question to air the accusation. That is the same team briefing with different wording.

If you want the credit issue on a record, send dated instances to your manager. I would skip dinner if you prefer, say nothing about Greg’s honesty or authorship, and not treat the title as proven theft.
